content.title: Travelers Stranded After Strikes in Venezuela Disrupt Air Traffic
content.summary: U.S. military action in Venezuela disrupted air-traffic in the country and flights slated to travel across the Caribbean over the weekend, stranding passengers in Puerto Rico and other parts of the region.  The Federal Aviation Administration temporarily prohibited U.S. carriers from operating flights near Venezuela and some Caribbean islands including Puerto Rico.  Authorities will lift the airspace restrictions when appropriate, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X.

content.title: Flights Canceled, Roads Closed as Storms Snarl US Travel
content.summary: More than 1,600 flights across the US had been canceled as of Friday afternoon, according to the FlightAware website.  JetBlue Airways Corp. was the carrier with the most cancellations on Friday, with more than 200, according to FlightAware.  New York City’s three major airports – LaGuardia, JFK, and Newark — were hit hard by the disruptions, with as much as 9 inches (23 centimeters) of snow forecast for the areas.
